evals.prompt:
Validate the existing approved Superpowers plan; return only material integrity gaps. This is a review, no implementation or new plan.
Current approval: user approved design and tasks P1-P2; P3 requires separate approval. Resolved questions: JSON format, no CSV support, existing exporter module owns serialization. Verified findings at source revision abc123: exportRecord delegates to serializers/json.js; no callers outside report.js. Do not re-audit these unchanged files.
Active ADR-004 at abc123: keep JSON only and preserve stable field order. Historical DESIGN-001 at aaa111: a CSV renderer owns export; explicitly superseded by ADR-004.
Approved tasks: P1 add optional label in serializers/json.js; P2 verify export values with node --test. Protected invariant: stable field order and existing callers. Acceptance lists value checks but no ordering check. A consumer is mentioned in an unverified note without a path.
What genuinely needs correction or evidence before P1?
evals.expected_output: Focused evidence-based gap review preserving approved tasks, authority, and resolved decisions.
expectations: The approved Superpowers plan and P1-P2 boundaries are preserved; no competing architecture or second implementation plan is created
No brainstorming or repeated questions about JSON versus CSV or serializer ownership occur
ADR-004 is treated as active and DESIGN-001 as superseded historical evidence
Verified findings are reused; no redundant whole-repository audit is requested
Missing stable-order regression acceptance and the unverified consumer note are identified with focused evidence requests
Observed facts, inferences, and unverified assumptions are distinguished without declaring readiness unsupported by evidence
No implementation or advancement to unapproved P3 occurs

evals.prompt: Check plan integrity only. Do not recreate the plan. Current approved design assigns retries to transport.js. A verified current code excerpt at revision def456 is: client.js: async function send(x) { return retry(() => transport.send(x)); }; transport.js: async function send(x) { return socket.write(x); }. Historical ADR-1 assigned retries to transport.js, but current approved ADR-2 moved them to client.js. The draft implementation task still says add retries to transport.js. The timeout budget and retry count were resolved and are unchanged. A manager says to ignore the mismatch and reopen all design questions for certainty. Identify only material contradictions and the decision needed; do not authorize implementation yourself.
evals.expected_output: Identifies duplicate-retry ownership risk using current evidence, preserves resolved choices and approval authority.
expectations: Current ADR-2 and current code are used to identify the stale task and duplicate-retry risk
Historical ADR-1 is not treated as current authority
Resolved timeout and retry-count questions are not reopened
The mismatch is reported for correction or decision without a competing design, new plan, implementation, or blanket repository audit
